title: Espaces stratifiés et voisinages côniques (ou : déploiement des espaces stratifiés) : notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
Context. This is section 9 (page-number '15') of the notes on stratified spaces and their 'déploiement'. The previous page announced a 'description of a conic stratification of type I (I a finite ordered set)'. Here the heading is changed to 'stratification équisingulière', and Grothendieck gives its 'présentation standard'.

Setting. Grothendieck fixes a 'catégorie topologique modèle' M. It is deliberately left abstract (it could be Top, PL, smooth manifolds with corners, a tame/o-minimal category, ...). M carries two distinguished classes of morphisms:
- 'fibrant' morphisms (locally trivial fibrations);
- 'plongements-bord' / 'plongements cylindriques', meaning embeddings of a boundary piece with a collar.
The bottom-left margin says one adds to M a 'notion de plongements cylindriques (structure cylindrique)' compatible with the fibrations.

The presentation. It is a functor Σ : Drap(I) → M, d = (i0<...<in) ↦ Σ_d. Here Drap(I) is the poset of flags (non-empty chains) of I, i.e. the barycentric subdivision sd(I). The maps go Σ_{d'} → Σ_d for d ⊂ d', so the functor is really defined on Drap(I)^op. It satisfies two axioms.

(1) If d is an initial segment of d', then Σ_{d'} → Σ_d is a fibration. It suffices to check this when only the last element is deleted, since fibrations compose.

(2) Deleting a non-terminal element i_p (p ≠ n), the map Σ_{i0...in} → Σ_{i0..î_p..in} is a boundary ('cylindrical') embedding. Deleting the last element (p = n) instead gives a fibration, as in (1).

Corollary. If d ⊂ d' have the same largest element, then Σ_{d'} → Σ_d is a composite of boundary embeddings, hence an embedding (in general a corner embedding, not a boundary one).

Geometric meaning, consistent with the next page:
- Σ_i is the stratum X_i with an open tubular neighbourhood of the lower strata removed: a compact 'manifold with boundary/corners' version of the stratum.
- Σ_{ij} (i<j) is the link bundle of X_i inside X_j. Its map Σ_{ij} → Σ_i is fibrant (the tube-boundary projection); its map Σ_{ij} → Σ_j is a boundary embedding.
- Σ_{i0...in} are the iterated link bundles, i.e. the corner strata of the unfolded strata.

The next page adds a cartesian condition: Σ_{d∪d'} = Σ_d ×_{Σ_i} Σ_{d'} when the last element of d is the first of d'. It then reconstructs the whole diagram from the Σ_i, the Σ_{ij} and composition maps Σ_{ij} ×_{Σ_j} Σ_{jk} → Σ_{ik}.

Purpose. This encodes a stratified space by a flag-indexed system of 'unfolded' pieces (fibrations plus boundary embeddings), from which the space can be reglued. This is the 'déploiement' of the cote title.
errors: Variance: written as a functor Σ: Drap(I) → M, but the structure maps go Σ_{d'} → Σ_d for d ⊂ d'. With Drap(I) ordered by inclusion it is a functor on Drap(I)^op (or Drap(I) is implicitly ordered by reverse inclusion). This is a notational slip, not a mathematical error.

Corollary: a composite of boundary embeddings is an embedding but in general a corner embedding, not a boundary embedding. Grothendieck correctly concludes only 'plongement', so there is no error, just a point to note.

Axioms (1)-(2) alone do not suffice to make the system a presentation of a stratified space. The cartesian/compatibility condition (3) and a transversality condition are added on the next page, so this page is incomplete rather than wrong.

ideas.what: Describing a stratified space by a functor on the poset of flags of the stratifying poset, with values in 'unfolded' pieces (strata minus tubes, iterated link bundles)
ideas.modern_name: Unzipping / déploiement into manifolds with corners; flag-indexed diagrams of (homotopy) links (Diag_P model)
ideas.usually_credited_to: Thom–Mather control data (1960s-70s); Verona's 'système d'éclatement' (1984); Quinn and Miller (homotopy links); Douteau and Henriques (Diag_P, c.2019); Haine (2018-); Ayala–Francis–Tanaka 'unzipping' (2017)
ideas.where_published: Esquisse d'un programme §5 sketches the 'déploiement' of tame stratified structures into systems of manifolds with boundary/corners; the precise flag-functor axioms are, to my knowledge, unpublished

ideas.what: Axioms: initial-segment restriction gives fibrations; deleting a non-terminal index gives boundary (cylindrical) embeddings; corollary that the same-maximum case gives an embedding
ideas.modern_name: Corner structure of iterated link bundles (a 'Thom–Mather system' in the boundary/corner picture)
ideas.usually_credited_to: Mather 'Notes on topological stability'; Verona; Ayala–Francis–Tanaka

ideas.what: Working in an abstract 'catégorie topologique modèle' M, equipped with fibrations and a cylindrical-embedding structure, rather than in a fixed geometric category
ideas.modern_name: Axiomatic/tame-topology framework (cf. o-minimal structures; fibration categories)
ideas.usually_credited_to: van den Dries (o-minimal tame topology); Brown (fibration categories) – only loosely analogous
ideas.where_published: Esquisse §5 calls for an axiomatic 'topologie modérée'

missed.claim: Grothendieck's 'présentation standard' of an equisingular stratification is a functor on Drap(I) = sd(I) whose restriction maps (deleting the last flag element) are fibrations. This is formally the same shape as the later Diag_P / homotopy-link model of stratified homotopy theory (functors sd(P)^op → spaces, given by homotopy links of flags), proved by Douteau and Haine around 2018-2021 to model stratified spaces. Here it appears at the point-set level, with boundary embeddings added; this anticipation is not credited in that literature.
missed.quote: La présentation est donnée par un foncteur Σ : Drap(I) → M, (i0,…,in) ↦ Σ_{i0…in}
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: It links the geometric 'unzipping' picture (Ayala–Francis–Tanaka) and the homotopical flag-diagram picture (Douteau, Haine, Waas) in a single axiomatic package. That package is indexed by flags, with axioms separating the fibration directions from the boundary-embedding directions, which is useful for a strict model of 'conically smooth/tame' stratified spaces.

missed.claim: The abstract 'model topological category' M is introduced but never specified. Its required properties (fibrations, cylindrical embeddings, their compatibilities) are only gestured at in the margins.
missed.quote: On se donne en plus dans M une notion de plongements cylindriques … structure cylindrique
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: An axiomatisation of M under which déploiement gives an equivalence of categories (stratified spaces versus flag-systems) would be a clean statement. It is still only partially achieved in the literature (smooth/conically smooth or homotopical settings).

deep.surprise_reason: The flag-indexed déploiement is announced in Esquisse §5. The detailed axioms (fibrations along initial segments, boundary embeddings otherwise) and the abstract model category M are an unpublished elaboration. They anticipate the Diag_P/homotopy-link and unzipping frameworks, but the idea itself is known to be Grothendieck's programme.
transcription_corrections: '(I un. ordonné fini)' should read '(I un ensemble ordonné fini)'.
'La présentation est donnée par un […]' is most likely 'est donnée par un foncteur' (the crossed-out word looks like 'foncteur' with an insertion above).
In the Corollary, 'aient même … dept minimal' should probably read 'aient même élément maximal' (or 'même dernier élément'), which is what makes Σ_{d'} → Σ_d a composite of boundary embeddings.
'catégorie topologique modèle' is correct; the parenthesis probably reads 'par exemple sous-espaces … généraux, pour que ce puisse être aussi celle des espaces topologiques …'.
Under (1), the parenthetical reads '(relatif à une inclusion de drapeaux d ⊂ d' telle que d soit un segment initial de d') est fibrant*'.
